import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 351

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/351](https://www.erdosproblems.com/351)
-/

open Polynomial

namespace Erdos351

/-- The set of rational numbers of the form `P(n) + 1 / n` where `n` is a natural number
and `P` is a polynomial with rational coefficients.

Note: We include `P 0` in there (since `1 / 0 = 0`), but this doesn't change the validity of the
conjecture -/
def imageSet {α : Type*} [Semifield α] (P : α[X]) : Set α :=
  Set.range (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ P.eval ↑n + 1 / n)

/-- The predicate that a set `A` is strongly complete, i.e. that for every finite set `B`, every sufficiently
large integer is a sum of elements of the set `A \ B`. -/
def IsStronglyComplete {α : Type*} [Semiring α] (A : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ B : Finset α,
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ↑m ∈ { ∑ n ∈ X, n | (X : Finset α) (_ : ↑X ⊆ A \ B) }

/-- The predicate that the rational polynomial `P` has a complete image. -/
def HasCompleteImage (P : ℚ[X]) : Prop := IsStronglyComplete (imageSet P)

/--
Let $p(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ be a non-constant rational polynomial with positive leading
coefficient. Is it true that $$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$ is strongly complete,
in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers? -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos351.lean"]
theorem erdos_351 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ P : ℚ[X], 0 < P.natDegree → 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P := by
  sorry

/--
Let $p(x) = x \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. It has been shown that
$$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$
is strongly complete, in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
protected theorem erdos_351.variants.X : HasCompleteImage X := by
  sorry

/-- Let $p(x) = x ^ 2 \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. It has been shown that
$$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$
is strongly complete, in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_351.variants.X_sq : HasCompleteImage (X ^ 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos351

reformulations.difference: The source allows every rational polynomial with positive leading coefficient; Lean additionally assumes `0 < P.natDegree`, excluding positive constants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted positive constants are independently strongly complete. Write c=a/b with positive integers a,b. After choosing a denominator threshold avoiding the finite deleted set, each r in {1,…,a} has distinct Egyptian-fraction expansions beyond that threshold with every sufficiently large number of terms. For a sufficiently large integer m=aq+r, choose an expansion of r with bq terms. The corresponding sum of c+1/n equals c·bq+r=m. Such arbitrary expansion lengths follow by repeatedly splitting the largest denominator d>1 using 1/d=1/(d+1)+1/(d(d+1)). Thus reinstating positive constants gives an equivalent universal assertion. Independently proved `constant_complete` and `main_iff_all_polynomials` in /workspace/review/constant.lean; neither depends on the theorem under review.

reformulations.difference: Its `imageSet` includes n=0, contributing P.eval 0 because Lean defines 1/0=0. The source's reciprocal expression uses positive indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The Lean image is exactly the positive-index image with the singleton {P.eval 0} adjoined. Strong completeness is invariant under adjoining one element: the forward direction deletes that element together with the arbitrary finite forbidden set; the reverse direction follows from monotonicity under inclusion. Proved `Review351.complete_image_iff_positive` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean for every rational polynomial.

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over `Finset ℚ` deletions and sufficiently large natural-number targets, whereas the source speaks of finite sets and sufficiently large integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite subset of ℚ has an equivalent Finset representation. Natural-number tails and integer tails give the same condition: choose a nonnegative threshold, then every integer above it is the cast of its natural-number value. The set-builder membership also unfolds to existence of a finite subset of A\B whose sum equals the target, with distinct values as required. Proved `Review351.strong_iff_source` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
